turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Welcome back, Dev. How are things feeling as you kick off the week?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hey Wren. Hanging in there, though honestly, sending resumes out into the void is starting to wear on me a bit.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Cold applications can really drain your energy. Have you thought about reaching out to someone in your network for an opening?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, actually, that crossed my mind today. My former teaching colleague Marcus works over at Ledgerly now, and I really want to see if he'd give me a referral.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That sounds like a great path to explore. How are you planning to open the conversation with him?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I was thinking of dropping him a note to say hi, and maybe share a link to my portfolio so he can see what I've been building.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Showing real work builds trust fast. Which project do you want him to see first?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Probably the bike-share one. I analyzed a public bike-share dataset in SQL for my portfolio, and the main thing I found was that weekend rides ran forty percent longer than weekday rides.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That metric sticks in the mind because it tells a simple story. How do you want to ask him for the referral itself?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll probably just ask if he has ten minutes for a quick phone catch-up first, and then bring up the open role naturally if it feels right.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Keeping it low-pressure makes it easy for him to say yes. When do you think you will send that note?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm planning to sit down and type it out right after we wrap up today.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Getting it out the door will feel good. Do you want to run through anything else before you write it?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No, I think I'm good to go. Talking it through gave me the nudge I needed.
